Any proposed lifecycle, pipeline, memory-layout, runtime-loader, data-order, numeric-policy, golden-boundary, or major template change after a fresh lifecycle-consistent board replay.
Any use of a rejected or contamination-barred artifact as validated evidence for backend, bitstream, runtime-ABI, or board-runtime promotion.

executable_actions.on_failure: If lifecycle-consistent observation cannot be derived solely from the already hash-bound exact source closure, or if reconciliation would require changing wrapper/DUT/selected simulation sources/semantic-testbench sources/checkpoint/stimulus/golden/weights/numeric policy, stop without edits. Do not rerun the connected kernel, do not run a board replay or dependent board gates, and do not promote.
executable_actions.rationale: Repair the invalid current-layer checker/observation capability, not hardware. Reconcile the existing exact-board trace against the live lifecycle policy: accepted ingress may precede lifecycle start, so kernel_start_precedes_stage0_input cannot remain a failing causal invariant. The resulting sidecar must preserve CCTG data-order, ready/valid, payload, transfer-count, direct-egress, and lifecycle obligations, bind every consumed artifact hash, record that the connected-kernel capability remains closed, and make no functional or numeric-pass claim.

observations: The board-layer functional_sim gate failed: all 16 input tokens and 1792 core-ingress beats were accepted, core egress was ready, and zero output beats were accepted. This is a real current-layer output-frontier symptom, not a functional pass or a proven RTL root cause.

The earliest normalized boundary failure asserts kernel_start_precedes_stage0_input at cycle 20572946, although the live hierarchical policy explicitly requires accepted input handshake before kernel lifecycle start and records lifecycle start at cycle 20572948. The existing observation contract is therefore internally inconsistent and its localization cannot yet justify a DUT, block_input, or stage0 repair.

The exact user-supplied wrapper identity and selected source closure are hash-bound and passed identity binding. Checkpoint, input stimulus, target-model expected output, numeric policy/tolerance, Transformer-block golden boundary, semantic-testbench source hash, and board-wrapper source hashes remain immutable for this repair loop.

The connected-kernel targeted replay is closed lower-layer evidence: it has a fresh VCS execution, 416 accepted trace records, complete 13-boundary liveness/order evidence, 1792 ingress and egress beats, terminal last, and required elastic cross-token overlap. No new valid current trace directly contradicts one of these certified invariants; it must not be requested, rerun, repaired, or reopened.

The failed board runtime-loader, output-count, data-order, DDR-roundtrip, AXI-protocol, and target-model numeric checks remain unproven because their dependent board gates are not_run. Loader completion of 1056 words and quiescent AXI transactions do not prove complete board weight consumption, output progress, lifecycle progress, or correct data order.

Active contamination barriers in sacg_memory_truth and open retry requests 0136, 0140, 0141, 0142, 0143, 0144, 0145, and 0146 are current downstream-consumption and promotion blockers. Rejected Stage7/Stage8 artifacts remain planning/debug evidence only until a fresh current-layer result is promoted; there are no open same-scope backtrack requests.
proposed_actions: Perform only a source-hash-bound, simulation-only reconciliation of the current exact-board lifecycle/CCTG observation contract. It must recognize pre-start accepted ingress as required behavior, retain all other boundary obligations, attest immutability, and emit a replay request rather than running a replay or changing hardware.
risks: Model/shape/numeric risk: no board output exists for the immutable target-model expected output, fp32/fp16 policy, or frozen comparison tolerance; reconciliation must not regenerate a golden or alter tolerance.

Data-order/memory/runtime risk: token/tile/lane/word ordering, loader schedule/address/data binding, complete-scope board-side tensor consumption, and DDR output roundtrip remain unproven. Independent AXI or prefetch progress cannot substitute for output-frontier evidence.

Implementation/board risk: modifying the exact wrapper, selected simulation closure, DUT RTL, semantic-testbench sources, checkpoint, stimulus, weights, or lifecycle architecture while correcting observability would invalidate the current source binding and requires explicit approval.

Verification risk: removing the contradictory pre-start assertion must preserve all valid ready/valid, payload, token-order, transfer-count, direct-egress, and lifecycle obligations; it must not mask the zero-egress symptom or claim hardware correctness.

Promotion risk: active SACG contamination barriers and open retries prohibit use of this failed run, reconciliation artifact, or any rejected retry as validated input for backend, implementation, bitstream, runtime-ABI, or board-runtime stages.

constraints: exact user-supplied board-wrapper and selected-source-closure hash immutability
